name: Jeroboam
description: King living at the time of United Monarchyand Divided Monarchy

points: Jeroboam the son of Nebat, Solomon's servant, a mighty man of valor, lifted up his hand against the king. Solomon had made him ruler over the charge of the house of Joseph, which was the two tribes Ephraim and Manasseh.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: The prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met Jeroboam in the way, took his new garment, rent it in twelve pieces, and gave Jeroboam ten, saying the Most High would rend ten tribes from Solomon's hand and give them to him. One tribe would remain for David's servant's sake and for Jerusalem, because Israel had forsaken the Most High and worshipped Ashtoreth, Chemosh, and Milcom.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: When Jeroboam and the people came the third day, Rehoboam answered roughly, forsaking the old men's counsel, and told them he would add to their yoke and chastise them with scorpions.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: The king hearkened not to the people, for the cause was from the Most High, that he might perform the saying he spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam; the prophecy had to come to pass.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: When Israel heard Jeroboam had returned, they called him to the congregation and made him king over Israel; none followed the house of David but the tribe of Judah only. That is how Jeroboam got the ten tribes.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: A man of God comes out of Judah by the word of the Most High and cries against Jeroboam's altar in Bethel while the king stands by it burning incense.

note.label: 1 Kings 13: The Man of God and the Two Prophets

points: The man of God out of Judah cried against the altar, and Jeroboam put forth his hand, saying, lay hold on him; and his hand dried up. You see how pain will get you to change your thoughts: he wanted to put the dude to death a few minutes ago, and now he wants him to pray to God for him. And the king's hand was restored.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

points: After all these signs, Jeroboam does not turn from his evil way but again makes priests of the high places from the lowest of the people.

note.label: 1 Kings 13: The Man of God and the Two Prophets

points: This thing becomes sin to the house of Jeroboam, enough to cut it off and destroy it from the face of the earth.

note.label: 1 Kings 13: The Man of God and the Two Prophets

points: When Jeroboam's son Abijah falls sick, the king tells his wife to disguise herself and go to Ahijah the prophet in Shiloh, carrying loaves, cakes, and honey to inquire about the child.

note.label: 1 Kings 14: Judgment on Jeroboam and the Reign of Rehoboam

points: Ahijah is old and blind, but the Most High tells him beforehand that Jeroboam's wife is coming feigning to be another woman.

note.label: 1 Kings 14: Judgment on Jeroboam and the Reign of Rehoboam

points: Ahijah tells the wife that when her feet enter the city, the child will die, and all Israel will mourn and bury him, for in him alone of Jeroboam's house is found some good thing toward the Most High.

note.label: 1 Kings 14: Judgment on Jeroboam and the Reign of Rehoboam

points: Jeroboam reigned twenty-two years, then slept with his fathers, and Nadab his son reigned in his place.

note.label: 1 Kings 14: Judgment on Jeroboam and the Reign of Rehoboam

points: There is continual war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam, and when Rehoboam dies, Abijam his son reigns in his place.

note.label: 1 Kings 14: Judgment on Jeroboam and the Reign of Rehoboam

points: Nadab son of Jeroboam reigns over Israel two years and does evil, walking in the way and sin of his father.

note.label: 1 Kings 15: Abijam, Asa, Nadab, and Baasha

points: Baasha conspires against him, kills him, and reigns in his place, then smites all the house of Jeroboam, leaving none that breathed, according to the word spoken by Ahijah the Shilonite.

note.label: 1 Kings 15: Abijam, Asa, Nadab, and Baasha

points: This fulfills, years later, the judgment that Jeroboam's descendants would be destroyed for the sins by which he made Israel to sin.

note.label: 1 Kings 15: Abijam, Asa, Nadab, and Baasha

points: The word of the Most High comes to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, because though he was exalted out of the dust and made prince over Israel, he walked in the way of Jeroboam and made Israel sin.

note.label: 1 Kings 16: Baasha to Ahab and the Rise of Baal Worship

points: Therefore the Most High will make his house like the house of Jeroboam, and those who die in the city the dogs will eat and those in the field the fowls will eat.

note.label: 1 Kings 16: Baasha to Ahab and the Rise of Baal Worship

points: His death comes for his sins in walking in the way of Jeroboam, and his treason is recorded, treason being punishable by death in that time.

note.label: 1 Kings 16: Baasha to Ahab and the Rise of Baal Worship

points: As if walking in Jeroboam's sins were a light thing, he takes Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians to wife and serves and worships Baal, rearing an altar and a grove, provoking the Most High more than all the kings before him. This mirrors Solomon, who followed Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and the marrying outside the people that the law forbids because it turns the heart to other gods.

note.label: 1 Kings 16: Baasha to Ahab and the Rise of Baal Worship

points: The Most High would bring evil on Ahab, cut off every male of his house, and make his house like the house of Jeroboam and the house of Baasha because of the provocation by which he made Israel to sin.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

points: Ahaziah the son of Ahab begins to reign over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat and reigns two years. He does evil in the sight of the Lord and walks in the way of his father and his mother and in the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: Nevertheless he cleaves to the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, and departs not from them. The house of Ahab had reared up images and led the kingdom into idolatry.

note.label: 2 Kings 3: Three Kings and the Water in the Ditches

points: Though Jehu destroys Baal out of Israel, he does not depart from the golden calves that Jeroboam set up in Bethel and in Dan; hold Dan in mind for later scriptures.

note.label: 2 Kings 10: Jehu Destroys Baal and Falls Short of the Law

points: Josiah also destroyed the altar and high place at Bethel that Jeroboam had made when he set up the golden calves, burning it and stamping it small to powder.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

points: The rest of the acts of Solomon are written in the book of Nathan the prophet, the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and the visions of Iddo the seer against Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: Rehoboam goes to Shechem where all Israel has gathered to make him king, and Jeroboam the son of Nebat returns out of Egypt where he had fled from Solomon.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: Jeroboam and the people return on the third day, and the king answers them roughly, forsaking the counsel of the old men and following the young men.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: The king does not listen to the people, for the cause was of the Most High, that the Lord might fulfill the word spoken by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: They obey the word of the Lord and return from going against Jeroboam, so the war between north and south does not happen.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 11: Rehoboam Strengthens Judah and the Levites Return

points: For Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest's office: they kicked Levi out. We don't want y'all here, cuz y'all trying to get us to do what God says. No, we want to worship idols. And Jeroboam ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: The priests and Levites out of all Israel resort to Rehoboam, leaving their suburbs and possessions to come to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam cast them off from the priest's office.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 11: Rehoboam Strengthens Judah and the Levites Return

points: The acts of Rehoboam are written in the book of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer concerning genealogies, and there were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: Abijah begins to reign over Judah in the eighteenth year of Jeroboam the first. War breaks out between Abijah and Jeroboam.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

points: Abijah sets the battle with 400,000 chosen men; Jeroboam answers with 800,000. Judah is outnumbered two to one, yet Abijah stands on the covenant of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

points: He names Jeroboam as the servant of Solomon who rose up and rebelled against his lord. To understand that rebellion, the account goes back to 1 Kings 11.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

points: Abijah warns the great multitude that trusts in the golden calves Jeroboam made and in the priests he ordained after the manner of the nations.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

points: Abijah pursues Jeroboam and takes cities from him. Jeroboam recovers no strength; the Most High strikes him and he dies.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant
